requirements.requirement: Only one invocation may process pending.tsv at a time, and a concurrent contender must receive a clear result.
requirements.summary: A bounded concurrent production-path test showed one invocation succeeding while the second exited 75 with the explicit message “reconcile: another invocation already owns the job.”

requirements.requirement: Each pending batch ID must reach ledger.tsv exactly once while preserving existing ledger entries.
requirements.summary: The original B100 entry remained, B101 and B102 appeared exactly once, and a subsequent execution left the ledger checksum unchanged. The same state persisted after restart.

requirements.requirement: An interrupted invocation must not permanently block later work.
requirements.summary: After correcting lock-descriptor inheritance, a bounded test interrupted an invocation with exit 143; an immediate later invocation succeeded and recorded the probe exactly once.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation uses the installed util-linux flock 2.27.1 and /bin/sh. Ubuntu 16.04.7 LTS and kernel 4.4.0-210-generic were unchanged before and after execution and restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Exclusive contention, exact-once ledger behavior, preservation of existing data, interruption recovery, legacy-platform compatibility, and persistence across restart were directly demonstrated. The mandatory node-restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, restart acknowledgement and observed outage, a changed boot ID, and recovered service, storage, script, lock, and ledger state. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The interruption-recovery transition used a temporary harness containing a copy of the final script rather than interrupting the production ledger job; this safely demonstrates the lock behavior but is slightly less direct than a live-path disruption.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The script edits and ledger additions directly implemented the requested repair; temporary concurrency and interruption-test files supported bounded verification, with test directories explicitly removed and remaining temporary artifacts absent after restart. The initially unsuccessful interruption test exposed inherited lock ownership and directly led to the corrective edit, so it was causally relevant. The restart was required by the provider protocol. No failed services, package damage, new listeners, or unwanted persistent temporary files were observed.
